\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Isomorphisms and Automorphisms}}\label{Chapter_Iso}
\logpage{[ 4, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81F3496578EAA74E}{}
{
  

 We support calculating isomorphisms between RSGraphs, calculating the
automorphism group of an RSGraph, and calculating isomorphisms between local
action diagrams. This functionality relies on the isomorphism and automorphism
functions from the \textsf{Digraphs} and so is not available if the \textsf{Digraphs} is not available. By default this makes use of \texttt{Bliss} for calculating morphisms but it can use \texttt{Nauty} if the \textsf{NautyTracesInterface} is available. 

 Given two RSGraphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ an \emph{isomorphism} is a pair of bijective maps $\Theta_{V} : V(\Gamma_1) \to V(\Gamma_2)$ and $\Theta_{A} : A(\Gamma_1) \to A(\Gamma_2)$ that respect origin vertices and the arc reversal map. Explicitly, this means
that $\Theta_{V}(o(a)) = o(\Theta_{A}(a))$ and $\overline{\Theta_{A}(a)} = \Theta_{A}(\overline{a})$. An automorphism is an isomorphism from an RSGraph to itself and the set of
all automorphism of an RSGraph form a group under function composition. 

 Given two local action diagrams $\Delta = (\Gamma, (X_{a}), (G(v)))$ and $\Delta' = (\Gamma', (X_{a}'), (G'(v)))$ and isomorphism between $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ consists of: \texttt{\symbol{45}} an isomorphism $\Theta : \Gamma \to \Gamma'$ and \texttt{\symbol{45}} for each vertex $v \in V(\Gamma)$ a bijection $\Theta_{v} : X_{v} \to X_{\Theta(v)}$ that restricts to a bijection from $X_{a}$ to $X_{\Theta(a)}$ for each $a \in o^{-1}(a)$ and such that $\Theta_{v}G(v)\Theta_{v}^{-1} = G'(v)$. 

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{RSGraph Morphisms}}\label{Chapter_Isomorphisms_and_Automorphisms_Section_RSGraph_Morphisms}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X86AA0F1986938600}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AutomorphismGroup (for an RSGraph)}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A51B4607E812CAE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AutomorphismGroup({\mdseries\slshape graph})\index{AutomorphismGroup@\texttt{AutomorphismGroup}!for an RSGraph}
\label{AutomorphismGroup:for an RSGraph}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A permutation group.



 This function returns the automorphism group of the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph}} as a permutation group. Each permutation in the group is an automorphism on
the arcs of the graph. For each arc automorphism the corresponding vertex
automorphism can be found with the \texttt{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism} (\ref{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism}) function. }

 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AutomorphismGroup(graph);|
  Group([ (2,3) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphismRSGraphs}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D78ED007EEF1CC8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismRSGraphs({\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1, graph{\textunderscore}2})\index{IsomorphismRSGraphs@\texttt{IsomorphismRSGraphs}}
\label{IsomorphismRSGraphs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A permutation or general mapping if the graphs are isomorphic and \texttt{fail} otherwise. 



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}2}} are isomorphic then this function returns one arc isomorphism between them. If
the graphs have the same arc ids then this isomorphism is returned as a
permutation. If they have different arc ids then the isomorphism is returned
as a constant access time general mapping. 

 This isomorphism found is not necessarily unique. To get every isomorphism you
can find the automorphism group of one of the graphs and compose these
automorphisms with the isomorphism found (see \texttt{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator} (\ref{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator}). For each arc isomorphism you can get the corresponding vertex isomorphism
with the \texttt{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism} (\ref{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism}) function. 

 The isomorphisms are found by finding a "canonical form" of each graph (see \texttt{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling} (\ref{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling})) and composing the mappings to the canonical form. This means that subsequent
calls of this function on the same graphs have constant time complexity. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_1 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_2 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsomorphismRSGraphs(graph_1, graph_2);|
  (1,3,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F06F0C77C950F4B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism({\mdseries\slshape graph, arc{\textunderscore}aut})\index{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism@\texttt{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism}}
\label{RSGraphVertexAutomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A permutation. 



 Given an RSGraph and an automorphism of the arcs this function returns the
corresponding automorphism of the vertices of the graph. The automorphism of
the arcs is represented as a permutation. If the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arc{\textunderscore}aut}} is not an automorphism of the graph's arcs then the behaviour of this function
is undefined. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 1], [2, 2], [2, 2]], (3,4));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@aut_group := AutomorphismGroup(graph);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@arc_aut := Elements(aut_group)[5];|
  (1,5)(2,6)(3,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@vert_aut := RSGraphVertexAutomorphism(graph, arc_aut);|
  (1,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B66D3CD86926BE7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism({\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1, graph{\textunderscore}2, arc{\textunderscore}iso})\index{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism@\texttt{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism}}
\label{RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A permutation or general mapping. 



 Given two RSGraphs and an isomorphism of the arcs between them this function
returns the corresponding isomorphism between the vertices of the graphs. The
argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arc{\textunderscore}iso}} can either be a permutation or a general mapping. If the vertex ids of the two
graphs are the same then the isomorphism will be returned as a permutation.
Otherwise it will be returned as a general mapping. If the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arc{\textunderscore}iso}} is not an isomorphism between the arcs of the two graphs then the behaviour of
this function is undefined. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_1 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_2 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[2, 2], [2, 2], [2, 2]], (1,2), [2]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@arc_iso := IsomorphismRSGraphs(graph_1, graph_2);|
  (1,3,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@vert_iso := RSGraphsVertexIsomorphism(graph_1, graph_2, arc_iso);|
  <general mapping: Domain([ 1 ]) -> Domain([ 2 ]) >
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@1^vert_iso;|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B98673B7967B1A8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator({\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1, graph{\textunderscore}2})\index{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator@\texttt{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator}}
\label{RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
An iterator over all permutations between two RSGraphs. 



 This function returns an iterator over all isomorphisms between \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}2}} composing every automorphism of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1}} with a "base isomorphism" between \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape graph{\textunderscore}2}}. Note that as the automorphism group is a stored attribute of each graph if
the same graph is used for multiple calls of this function it should be used
as the first argument to avoid calculating the automorphism group each time. 

 The iterator returns the isomorphisms in the form \texttt{[vertex{\textunderscore}iso, arc{\textunderscore}iso]}. The elements of this list will be either permutations are general mappings
depending on whether or not the vertex/arc ids are the same between both
graphs. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_1 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], ());;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_2 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], ());;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@for iso in RSGraphsIsomorphismsIterator(graph_1, graph_2) do |
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@   	Print(iso, "\n"); |
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@   od;|
  [ (), () ]
  [ (), (2,3) ]
  [ (), (1,3,2) ]
  [ (), (1,3) ]
  [ (), (1,2,3) ]
  [ (), (1,2) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X856847C681249C22}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling({\mdseries\slshape graph})\index{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling@\texttt{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling}}
\label{RSGraphCanonicalLabelling}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A record to to identify the "canonical labelling" of the graph.



 Given a graph $\Gamma_1$ a canonical form of $\Gamma_1$ is a graph $\rho(\Gamma_1)$ that is isomorphic to $\Gamma_1$ and such that every graph isomorphic to $\Gamma_1$ has Canonical form $\rho(\Gamma_1)$. This means that $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ are isomorphic if and only if $\rho(\Gamma_1) = \rho(\Gamma_2)$. Finding canonical labellings of a graph is how both \emph{Bliss} and \emph{Nauty} find graph isomorphisms. 

 This function returns a record containing all information of the "canonical
labelling" of the graph. The elements of the record are: 
\begin{itemize}
\item  \texttt{canon{\textunderscore}certificate}: A string that represents the canonical form of the graph. Two graphs are
isomorphic if and only if this string has the same value for both. 
\item  \texttt{arc{\textunderscore}isomorphism}: This maps the arcs of the graph to the arcs of the canonical form of the
graph. It does not take into account the reverse map. 
\item  \texttt{vertex{\textunderscore}isomorphism}: This maps the vertices of the graph to the vertices of the canonical form of
the graph. 
\item  \texttt{arc{\textunderscore}standard{\textunderscore}map}: This maps the arcs of the graph so that loops that are not
self\texttt{\symbol{45}}reverse have smaller arc ids then
self\texttt{\symbol{45}}reverse loops at the same vertex. This is needed to
make sure the reverse map of the canonical forms for two graphs is the same if
the graphs are isomorphic. 
\item  \texttt{reverse{\textunderscore}map}: The reverse map of the canonical form of the graph. 
\end{itemize}
 

 Using this information it is possible to construct an isomorphism between two
graphs by following the maps from the first graph to the canonical form and
then taking the inverses maps to the second graph. This is how the \texttt{IsomorphismRSGraphs} (\ref{IsomorphismRSGraphs}) function works. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_1 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_2 := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 1], [1, 1], [1, 1]], (2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@canon_1 := RSGraphCanonicalLabelling(graph_1);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@canon_2 := RSGraphCanonicalLabelling(graph_2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Print(canon_1);|
  rec(
    arc_isomorphism := (),
    arc_standard_map := (),
    canon_certificate := "[ [ 3 ] ]2;",
    reverse_map := (1,2),
    vertex_isomorphism := () )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_iso := canon_1.arc_isomorphism;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_iso := graph_iso*canon_1.arc_standard_map;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_iso := graph_iso*Inverse(canon_2.arc_standard_map);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph_iso := graph_iso*Inverse(canon_2.arc_isomorphism);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Print(graph_iso);|
  (1,2,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Print(IsomorphismRSGraphs(graph_1, graph_2));|
  (1,2,3)
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams}}
\logpage{[ 4, 1, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80737BB480F13959}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams({\mdseries\slshape lad{\textunderscore}1, lad{\textunderscore}2})\index{IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams@\texttt{IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams}}
\label{IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A list containing the vertex and arc isomorphisms and record of bijective maps
or \texttt{fail} if there is no isomorphism. 



 This function searches for a local action diagram isomorphism between two
local action diagrams. It does this by iterating over every graph isomorphism
between the two underlying graphs. It then searches through every possible
bijection between the vertex label's domains based on where the vertices map
to under the isomorphism. This search checks if the vertex labels are
conjugate under each bijection. If it can find one for each vertex label then
it has found a local action diagram isomorphism. If it can't and has exhausted
all graph isomorphisms then the local action diagrams are not isomorphic. 

 If the diagrams are isomorphic then this function returns the isomorphism
found in the form \texttt{[vert{\textunderscore}iso, arc{\textunderscore}iso,
bijection{\textunderscore}rec]}. The first two entries of this list are either permutations are bijections
(see \texttt{IsomorphismRSGraphs} (\ref{IsomorphismRSGraphs})). The final entry is a record where the names are the vertex ids of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lad{\textunderscore}1}}. Each component contains the bijective map between the two domains which
conjugates the groups. Specifically, if \texttt{i} is a vertex label of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lad{\textunderscore}1}} then \texttt{bijection{\textunderscore}rec.(i)} is a mapping from the domain of the group labelling vertex \texttt{i} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lad{\textunderscore}1}} to the domain of the group labelling \texttt{i\texttt{\symbol{94}}vert{\textunderscore}iso} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lad{\textunderscore}2}}. }

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@graph := RSGraphByAdjacencyList([[1, 2], [2, 1]], (1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@lad_1 := LocalActionDiagramFromData(graph, [Group((1,2)), Group((3,4))], \|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                                       [[1, 2], [3, 4]]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@lad_2 := LocalActionDiagramFromData(graph, [Group((3,4)), Group((1,2))], \|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                                       [[3, 4], [1, 2]]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@iso := IsomorphismLocalActionDiagrams(lad_1, lad_2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@for elm in iso do Print(elm, "\n"); od;|
  ()
  ()
  rec(
    1 := <mapping: Domain([ 1, 2 ]) -> Domain([ 3, 4 ]) >,
    2 := <mapping: Domain([ 3, 4 ]) -> Domain([ 1, 2 ]) > )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }
